title: Building Agent Session Insights: player, reviewer, and repository

interpretation.summary: This is the GitHub Copilot CLI conversation that built Agent Session Insights itself: a reusable reviewer, an interactive player, and a private GitHub repository. The scope starts with the sessionreviewer design request and ends with the completed repository push, excluding earlier prompt recovery and later Pages setup. It includes 12 typed prompts and three genuine form answers. Human direction determines the multi-harness scope, fixed Venn theme, navigation, accounting, information hierarchy, reproducible example, privacy and project name. Historical replies mentioning 22 prompts, 176 requests or $12.587361 describe the earlier Codex fixture used during development, not this Copilot session's measured usage. Historical delivery and test claims remain agent-reported; this run independently verifies the newly generated report and player.

decisions.title: Turn a one-off replay into a reusable reviewer
decisions.analysis: The human requests a standalone sessionreviewer directory, agent skills and prompts, collection across five harnesses, analysis, an HTML/PDF report and a standalone player. The response reports implementing the package and testing it on the earlier creation-session fixture. The requested product is a report of agent work, not merely a raw trace viewer.

decisions.title: Preserve the existing Venn visual framework
decisions.analysis: This recorded form answer selects the existing Venn report/player design. The assistant confirms it will preserve that framework. The theme is fixed; the later clarification distinguishes log-driven content and metrics from dynamically generated visual design.

decisions.title: Use direct manipulation for transcript and timeline navigation
decisions.analysis: The human specifies arrow buttons on the right, click-and-drag zoom and a scrollbar. This replaces a vague zoom requirement with concrete interaction behavior. The assistant reports right-aligned arrows, drag selection and scroll-based panning; the new publishing checks independently exercise those controls.

decisions.title: Make model usage and resource costs inspectable
decisions.analysis: The human asks for models, estimated session spend, spend within the zoomed region, and per-turn input/output tokens and cost. The response distinguishes the fixed theme from computed content and reports adding cache-aware historical API-equivalent estimates. The dollar amount quoted in that historical response belongs to the old Codex test fixture; this report computes a separate estimate for the selected Copilot requests.

decisions.title: Attach costs to prompts instead of duplicating summary cards
decisions.analysis: The human rejects the space used by competing full-session and zoom summaries. The requested hierarchy puts the total in one place and attaches model, input/output tokens and cost to each human prompt, including the full log. The response reports a compact totals strip and prompt footers in the player and complete HTML/PDF record.

decisions.title: Package a reproducible repository with an embedded example
decisions.analysis: The human requests a Git repository, a README explaining how to run this session, an embedded player and a paper link. The assistant reports a local repository and a clean-checkout reproduction. The bundled example initially used the earlier Codex development fixture; this corrected example now contains the Copilot conversation that built the package and repository.

decisions.title: Make the paper a meta-report about the project
decisions.analysis: The form answer explicitly asks for a paper generated for this session, a meta-report for the project, rather than the original cross-harness study. The response agrees to include a creation-session paper alongside the HTML report and embedded replay. This clarification establishes the intended subject of the example.

decisions.title: Keep the repository private and resolve the name before pushing
decisions.analysis: The recorded form answer selects private visibility and pauses repository naming for suggestions. The subsequent conversation explores alternatives before the final approval. The final response reports a push to the private agent-session-insights repository. This is a genuine human decision captured through a form, not a synthetic harness instruction.

decisions.title: Set a practical threshold for naming conflicts
decisions.analysis: The human requires conflict searches but excludes projects with fewer than 100 stars from disqualifying a name. The assistant applies that criterion to further suggestions. Search results and star counts are historical agent reports; this replay does not claim that they remain current.

decisions.title: Name the analysis product rather than the underlying trace
decisions.analysis: The human asks for session, analysis, insights and summary terminology, explicitly distinguishing a report of a trace from the trace itself. The response shifts the proposed names toward readable reports and findings. This reframes the product rather than merely choosing a label.

decisions.title: Choose Agent Session Insights and authorize the branded repository
decisions.analysis: The human proposes AgentSessionInsights and then approves proceeding in H015. The assistant agrees to the display name Agent Session Insights and reports rebranding the paper/player and pushing the private repository. The selected interval ends with that delivery response, before the later GitHub Pages discussion.

cost: Estimated API-equivalent total: $5.665353 USD. 120 of 120 observed requests priced. Frozen rate card dated 2026-11-07; not an actual bill.

pricing.basis: Standard global API-equivalent token processing; not actual harness subscription spend

gpt-5.4-nano.note: No writes recorded; unused write rate is ordinary input rate.

gpt-4o-mini.note: No writes recorded; unused write rate is ordinary input rate.

gpt-6-luna.note: Added for the 2026-11-08 update; standard short-context rates and the 272K long-context rule confirmed on both the model page and the standard pricing table. The 30-minute write rate is used, as for the other Codex OpenAI models.

pricing.verified_on_by_model_note: All other rates were verified on 2026-11-07; gpt-6-luna was verified on 2026-11-08.
assumptions: Reprice the frozen cohort at verified public standard global API rates, regardless of actual subscription, provider or priority tier.

Claude Code raw requests expose five-minute cache writes and standard speed; Copilot exposes 300-second Claude writes and 1800-second Sol writes. The same short-TTL policy is assumed for SQL-only Copilot records without surviving policy fields.
Use normalized request input tokens including cache read/write to test the 272000-token OpenAI threshold. Apply 2x to all input components and 1.5x to all output on qualifying requests.
Codex records do not expose cache-write TTLs (no cache writes are recorded for Codex); gpt-6-luna uses the same 30-minute write rate convention as the other OpenAI models.
No generic utility model substitution. Missing browser usage remains unpriced.
Exclude subscriptions, credits, tool fees, compute/GPU, storage, taxes, discounts, regional premiums and fast-mode premiums. This estimate does not reconstruct an invoice.
pricing.method: Inclusive input is split into fresh, cached-read and cache-write tokens. Apply the supplied model rates and long-context multipliers per request; output already includes reasoning. Estimates exclude subscriptions, tools, compute, taxes and discounts.

And add some things to th eplayer: a forward back buttons by the session text view, zoom abaility and time on the timeline axis. Then run it on the same creation playback logs so that I can see how it comes out. Put the generated report/player in a temp directory under the root of this project
next and back need to be arrow button on the right. Zoom should be interactive click and drag and have scrollbar
is the "venn design" dynamically generated based on the session logs. Player should include model uses, estimated total spend, spend in the zoomed area, and spend by turn, including tokens in/out.

review the UX to streamline. Too much space on zoomed vs total. Total should be in one place. And cost for session text should show model and cost input/output tokens attached to the user prompt, not at the top. Costs should also be showin on the fill session log
okay, create a git repo for this, make sure that the readme describes how to run it with this specific session log as the example with the embedded player and a link ot the paper in the repo for it.
suggest a name for the project. give me 3 names
look to see if anyone else is using that name
come up with 3 more, after you've done conflict searches. If the conflict has < 100 stars then it's not a conflict
come up wiht a few more. I like "session", "analysis",  "insights", "summary", etc. type names to more directly capture that this isn't a trace, its a report of a trace

limitations: Observed log coverage is not a guarantee of complete project history.
Input totals include cached input; reasoning output is not counted a second time.
Metered usage is not a subscription bill or evidence of comparative model quality.

Per-input request ownership uses recorded turn IDs when available, otherwise inferred same-conversation proximity. Missing/unmatched inputs remain unattributed; turn costs cover complete recorded turns, not just elapsed playback.
Occupied bins are not working hours, runtime, latency, or proof of unattended work.
Historical assistant completion claims are agent-reported, not independently verified here.
Pasted or AI-drafted user material does not establish original authorship.
Unknown timestamps remain outside the timeline; tool payloads and internal reasoning are not displayed.
Credential redaction is best effort; private outputs require review before sharing.
